title: The Core Mass Function in the Massive Protocluster G286.21+0.17 Revealed by ALMA
question: What is the core mass function of the massive protocluster G286.21+0.17 from 1.3 mm ALMA continuum, and how does it compare with the Salpeter IMF and depend on core-finding method?

data.arrays: 12-m array and 7-m array (plus total power for lines)
data.sensitivity: 1σ 0.45 mJy/beam in central strip; 0.2–0.46 mJy/beam range

what.value: Dust opacity 0.899 cm2/g at 1.3 mm (Ossenkopf & Henning moderately coagulated thin ice mantle model)

evidence.quote: (moderately coagulated thin ice mantle model of Ossenkopf & Henning 1994)

recipe.method: Pipeline-calibrated 7-m and 12-m data imaged with tclean, Briggs weighting, with and without uvtaper
Dendrogram (leaves) and clumpfind with fiducial Fmin=4σ, δ=1σ or Δ=3σ, Smin=0.5 beam; parameters varied
Optically thin dust emission: M = 0.192 (F/mJy)(d/2.5 kpc)^2 Msun
assumptions: Td = 20 K uniform; kappa_1.3mm,d=0.899 cm2/g; gas-to-dust 141; d=2.5 kpc

recipe.method: Artificial core insertion (10 beam-shaped cores per run, 30 repeats) to get flux and number recovery fractions
assumptions: Artificial cores have synthesized-beam shape; positions random scaled to 7-m flux profile

recipe.method: Power law dN/dlogM ∝ M^-α fit to bins above 0.8 Msun, 5 bins per dex, chi2 in log space

answer_key.quantity: Fiducial dendrogram true CMF slope α (M>0.8 Msun)

evidence.quote: while that for the fully (flux and number) corrected, i.e., “true”, CMF yields $\alpha=1.24\pm0.17$

answer_key.quantity: Fiducial clumpfind true CMF slope α

evidence.quote: identifies 76 cores, while the fiducial clumpfind method

answer_key.quantity: Dendrogram true CMF slope for M>0.3 Msun

evidence.quote: we derive a moderately shallower value of $\alpha=0.83\pm0.11$

answer_key.quantity: Number of dendrogram cores for Fmin=3σ

evidence.quote: We estimate that we are about 50% complete by number for $\sim1\:M_\odot$ cores.
